text:
Tara: FYI - Customer ticket #C-9421 just escalated. Dashboard export is truncating after ~10k tokens for some large-batch jobs. CS says multiple customers hit it after launch. Need to decide hotfix vs scheduled rework.

Diego: It's affecting three paying customers, one is on Dedicated. They want either an immediate workaround or a promise of a fix timeline.

Sam: What's the root cause short summary?

Nina: Looks like an integer overflow in the chunking iterator when export rows > 65535. Reproducible locally.

Sam: Overflow -> small code patch likely. But exports touch streaming + storage pipeline. Quick fix could be a bounds check and chunking change. Risk: if we change chunk logic, might affect consumers of streaming order.

Raj: From design POV we should keep CSV schema stable. Any fix must not reorder rows.

Tara: Two options: A) emergency patch that adjusts chunking limits and adds guardrails (estimated 1 dev-day + 0.5 QA), or B) larger rework to move export to async export-job backed by S3 with full retries and guarantees (est 2 sprints).

Diego: Customers will accept a short-term patch if we commit publicly to the rework. They want ETA for the robust solution.

Sam: Proposed plan: ship a non-invasive hotfix this sprint to stop the truncation. Parallel: open an epic for async export with specs and run discovery next week. Hotfix flagged as low-risk and feature-flagged for canary.

Nina: QA note: hotfix needs a small e2e that simulates ~1M token export. We'll need a long-run test in CI but can gate the canary to one customer first.

Raj: Also, add an acceptance criteria: exported CSV must match source ordering + no silent row drops. Include a checksum validation in export tool.

Tara: Communication: we tell customers "hotfix rolling out in 48h, followed by durable export in 4 weeks for beta, GA in 8 weeks". Is that realistic?

Sam: 48h for canary rollout + monitoring is doable. 4 weeks to have a beta async export is optimistic but fine if we scope MVP narrowly (S3 job + retry + indexing). 8 weeks GA might need more infra work.

Diego: I'll message the customers with that timeline and offer a manual workaround (split batches) until canary completes.

Sam: Risk list: race on streaming consumers, DB load on async job, cost of S3 exports. We'll add throttling and a per-tenant concurrency cap.

Nina: Add QA gating: Canary run 72h with metrics: success rate >= 99.5% and zero data mismatch. If fails, rollback and escalate.

Tara: OK owners: Sam -> hotfix PR, Nina -> test matrix + canary checklist, Raj -> CSV checksum design + doc, Diego -> customer comms and support ticket updates, Tara -> epic & roadmap placement.

deploy-bot: Build queued: release/2.3.4-hotfix -> staging.canary -> flag: `--canary-tenant=dedicated-42`.

Sam: I'll land a small patch branch `hotfix/export-truncate` and include defensive tests.

Raj: I'll drop a minimal spec in Confluence and include error examples + checksum pseudo-code.

Diego: CS will prepare a templated message for customers and CS/AE handoff notes.

Tara: Roadmap action: mark async-export epic as "high" priority but split into two milestones: MVP (basic S3 export + retries), then Reliability+Performance. Estimate MVP ~3 dev-weeks. We'll staff next sprint with one eng and one infra.

Sam: Agree. Tagging the epic with infra touchpoints; will need infra review.

Nina: I'll add the long-run CI job to nightly to catch regressions.

Tara: Decision recap: ship hotfix canary in 48h -> observe 72h -> full rollout if metrics good. Meanwhile run discovery and start MVP epic for async export with a 4-week beta target. Customer comms prepared.

Diego: Sounds good. I'll update ticket C-9421 and ping customers.

Sam: Starting PR now.

Tara: Thanks all. If the canary shows any data mismatch, move to incident and loop in eng-sre.
